candidates.title: Meta Muse: personal AI agents reshape consumer trust debate
candidates.why: First-wave consumer personal AI agent forces developers to confront permission architecture — Meta's demand for email/calendar/payment access shows how agent capability collides with user trust, core design question for any agent system.
candidates.local_angle_potential: Meta's permission model raises strategic question: how should regional platforms balance agent capability with local user trust expectations? Regulatory/cultural context differs from US, making design choices consequential.

candidates.title: OpenAI agents: from research boom to working applications
candidates.why: Autonomous agent systems graduating from research announcements to real applications (family scheduler built with Astra). Practical patterns matter more than theoretical advances for developer adoption.
candidates.local_angle_potential: Developer teams can apply autonomous patterns (task orchestration, multi-step planning) from research to local workflow automation projects; concrete architecture shifts become foreseeable.

candidates.title: ChatGPT Images 2.5 brings personalization to image generation
candidates.why: Feature improvement, not new model — reference photos/sketches → more personalized outputs. Tool adoption matters more than model announcements for working developer teams.
candidates.local_angle_potential: For teams with any visual content workflow (UI prototyping, marketing assets, design iteration): Images 2.5 changes generation speed. Worth testing if your stack touches image generation.

items.title: Creepy crawlies
items.summary: Creepy crawlies Konstantin Ryabitsev discusses how bad the "background radiation" of abusive crawlers has become from the perspective of git.kernel.org , the official Git repository for the Linux kernel: TL;DR: we spend more CPU cycles rendering commits for scrapers than we spend on all other kinds of legitimate access, including git clones. At any one time, across 5 geo-distributed nodes, there are 14 CPU cores doing nothing but rendering git commits as html. I worry about this a lot from the perspective of Datasette, which serves a huge number of crawlable web pages. Via Hacker News Tags: cr
